candidates.name: A — Journal-scored field protocol (real phone, real rooms, ground-truth turn log)
candidates.sketch: Instrument the shipped pipeline: a new ListenJournal event records per-line {tag, best score, runner-up, owner score, seconds of audio} — numbers only, never text/audio/embeddings — plus the missing Settings export (ShareLink of entries). Then a pre-registered protocol: owner + one consenting other, build 76 by cable, five conditions (quiet table, kitchen noise, phone-in-pocket, outdoors, Google-Meet-at-speaker-volume — the Tejas condition), ~10 scripted alternating turns each, enrolled via the real VoiceEnrollView. A scorer (proof/voice_live_score.py) joins exported journal to the turn log, computes coverage, false-owner (must be 0), owner-recall, other-consistency per condition, writes RESULTS.json into research/evals/voice-live-<date>/, and cross-checks LIVE prod events.speaker rows for the session window against the journal. A new red gate leg holds until the artifact exists and meets floors declared BEFORE recording.
candidates.pros: Measures the pipeline that actually ships — real mouth-to-mic geometry, ring buffer, converter, real acoustics; ground truth for the one metric that kills the product (false-owner); produces a repo artifact a gate can hold red (Laws 3+4); pre-registered floors resist polishing the red line (Brief §0); ~3 focused days plus one hour of a second human; the same journal instrument becomes the permanent field diagnostic.
candidates.cons: One phone, two voices, one hour — establishes floors and catches catastrophe, never certifies (the scale trap); needs a cable-installed build (cluster F); needs a second human scheduled; scores in an owner-exported journal are new (benign — scalars, owner-tap export, but must be argued in review).

candidates.name: B — Loudspeaker replay bench (curated recordings played at the phone)
candidates.sketch: Record a two-voice ground-truth conversation once on any device; replay it through a loudspeaker at the enrolled phone in several rooms; same journal instrument and scorer as A. Fully repeatable — rerun after any model/threshold change with zero human scheduling.
candidates.pros: Repeatable regression harness; one human total; perfect ground truth alignment; can sweep volumes/distances mechanically.
candidates.cons: A loudspeaker is not a mouth: coloration, single point source, no head movement — it measures speaker-through-air, and enrollment-vs-playback mismatch can bias owner scores either way. Honest as a REGRESSION bench after live proof exists, dishonest as the live proof itself. Roughly the same build cost as A without answering A's question.

candidates.name: C — Passive production week (telemetry only, no script)
candidates.sketch: Ship just the journal instrument, let the owner live normally for a week, then measure coverage and score distributions from exported journal + prod events.speaker rates; owner annotates a few remembered conversations after the fact.
candidates.pros: Zero protocol cost; the most real conditions possible; coverage (the 97%-no-verdict question) is measurable with no ground truth at all — worth doing continuously after proof.
candidates.cons: No ground truth means false-owner — the killer metric — is unmeasurable; post-hoc human annotation of who spoke when is memory, not measurement; takes a calendar week; fails the 'until proven, what may the brain trust' question entirely. Complement to A, not a substitute.

candidates.name: D — Cloud shadow diarization (REFUSED)

candidates.pros: Automatic labels at scale; no scripted session.
candidates.cons: Raw audio leaving the phone violates the local-first law and the never-build list (cloud voiceprints; 'voiceprints and raw audio never leave the phone — law, not preference'). Named only to be refused — no claimed purpose exempts it.

law_notes: Law 1: untouched — no code that decides meaning changes; the IPA audit's symbol/manifest matching is deterministic gate-side pattern-matching on build artifacts, squarely inside the senses/gates carve-out. Law 2: no TAPE introduced — the strip script is a permanent, root-caused build step (Xcode ≥15.3 copies static SPM framework bundles; ours are invalid stubs), documented in-line and watched by a gate leg that fails if the bundles ever reappear or if the audit's premise shifts under a new Xcode; nothing here has an expiry because nothing here is a guess. Law 3: the definition of done is Apple's own API saying VALID plus a real TestFlight install — repo-green (a clean archive) is explicitly not accepted, mirroring is_it_live.py. Law 4: the b47-b50 experiment that cracked this lived in HANDOFF-2026-08-08.md, which is why it was recoverable — the new gates and this design land as repo files the same way. Law 5: this is a senses fix (she ships with working ears for who is speaking) done before any structural alternative (B's dynamic linking, C's vendoring) — and it un-blocks the on-device speaker path, which is what keeps the Never-build line (voiceprints and raw audio never leave the phone) holdable in shipped builds rather than only on cable-installed ones. Law 6: adversarial passes applied — the gate is mutation-tested so it cannot be a test that cannot fail; the audit asserts sherpa symbols are PRESENT so the fix cannot pass by regressing to build ≤75's empty link; and the b49 'privacy manifest disproved' claim was itself re-attacked and shown to have tested an incomplete manifest. Never-build: no always-streaming firmware, no cloud voiceprints, no fine-tuning, no rewrite — B (a packaging change) was considered and rejected on cost, not built.
